data.name: Muthanna
data.gender_notes: Muthanna is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Muthanna is an Arabic name derived from the word muthanna which means 'reviver' or 'renewer'. It is a name given to those who bring renewal, revival, and rejuvenation in their respective fields or communities. In Islamic history, Muthanna ibn Haritha was a companion of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and played a significant role in the Battle of the Trench.
data.spiritual_meaning: Bringing renewal and revival in one's life and in the world.
data.etymology: Muthanna belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Reviver, Renewer.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Muthanna total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: Muthanna is a name that holds historical significance in Islamic culture. The name was given to Muthanna ibn Haritha, who was a prominent figure during the early Islamic era. He was one of the ten Companions who were given the title "Those given to the shield," which signified their bravery and loyalty to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Muthanna participated in the Battle of the Trench, which was a major turning point in Islamic history, and was instrumental in the defeat of the invading Byzantine and Persian forces. The name Muthanna has since been associated with strength, courage, and resilience in the face of adversity.
data.spiritual_significance: Muthanna, as a name, also carries spiritual significance. The root of the name means 'reviver' or 'renewer'. This signifies that those who bear this name are called to bring renewal, revival, and rejuvenation in their respective fields or communities. As Muslims, we believe that every individual has a role to play in the betterment of society, and the name Muthanna serves as a reminder of this. It is a call to be a source of positivity and inspiration, to breathe new life into situations and to bring about change for the better. Furthermore, the name is a reminder of the Prophet Muthanna (as), who revived and renewed the faith of the people during a time of hardship and uncertainty. Thus, the name Muthanna holds both cultural and spiritual significance as a symbol of courage, resilience, and renewal.
